messages.content:
You are the writer of the discussion described below. You write out the discussion that the participants listed below take part in, under the rules and the flow given.

## Setting
Choosing where the group travels. Five friends take one trip together each year and have reached the point where the destination must be fixed. Everyone is going regardless of which is chosen. Participants: Victoria, Toshio, Daisuke, Sakura and Midori. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Pricing of offshore houses let whole
- Valley inn rates versus urban beds
- Ferry sailings and train time
- Getting around by train and bus
- Bathing hours and bathroom provision
- Inn mealtimes and room arrangements
- All-in rates against meals bought separately
- What separately booked rooms cost last time
- Time alone in the shared-house year
- How last year's days ran

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Sakura, Victoria, Midori, Toshio and Daisuke. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the options | 4 turns | every participant votes; the option with the most votes is adopted |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied options is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

## Participants

Gender: female

She is reserved in her emotional expressions and keenly observes the expressions and attitudes of others, trying to discern their inner thoughts. Because she does not express herself much, she often gives others the impression of being somewhat mysterious, but deep down she has a strong will and a determination to stick to her beliefs. At times, she may display expressions of anxiety or fear, but it is precisely in such moments that her true strength becomes evident.
Concern: Whatever we settle on, the bill always lands differently from what I pictured when I agreed to it, and by then there is nothing to be done. I would rather know what the whole week costs before we commit than find it out in instalments.

It seems that he has experienced some pain or suffering in his past, but he rarely shows it to others, and those scars may be connected to his cold-hearted side.
Concern: Every year the getting there swallows a day at each end, and I come home needing a rest from the holiday. What I mind is not the distance so much as how much of the week goes on arranging, moving and waiting.

He has a quiet personality, and occasionally his emotions become overwhelming, leading to periods of low mood. However, as he becomes able to rely on those around him, he gradually regains his composure.

She values balance in both her work and personal life and places importance on harmony with those around her.
Concern: The point of these weeks is the five of us together, yet the last few have left me feeling either crowded or oddly alone, and never for a reason I could name at the time. Before we book anything I would like to understand what actually produces that.

## Hidden information
The options and the full text of every card are listed here. The participants do not know them before the schedule above says so, and nothing from them may appear in the talk before the round in which it is revealed.

Options (see the schedule above):
- A: Island Trip. A stay on an offshore island reached by ferry, with the group in one rented house and transport on the island arranged as a group.
- B: City Break. Several nights in a large city with separate accommodation and a loose plan, leaving each person to arrange their own daytime routes.
- C: Hot Spring Town. A stay at an inn in a spa town reachable by train, with meals taken at the inn and the days left unplanned.

Cards (see the schedule above; title: text):
- Pricing of offshore houses let whole: Houses out on the islands let by the building rather than the head: the ones that were priced come to about 5,400 yen a head a night, with food on top.
- Valley inn rates versus urban beds: Inn rates in that valley sit near 17,000 yen a head with dinner and breakfast folded in; a city bed alone runs 12,000 to 20,000, and meals come after that.
- Ferry sailings and train time: The ferry sails three times a day and the last one back leaves at 16:20, so two days go to travelling; the train up to the spa valley takes ninety minutes.
- Getting around by train and bus: A city runs on trains every few minutes, so nobody has to plan ahead to move; the bus out of the spa valley goes hourly and stops before seven in the evening.
- Bathing hours and bathroom provision: Inn baths open from before six in the morning until midnight; the island houses examined list one bathroom for the whole building, and reviews mention the water running cold.
- Inn mealtimes and room arrangements: Dinner at those inns is served at six and breakfast at half seven, with everyone on futons in one room; a city room has a door and no timetable.
- All-in rates against meals bought separately: An all-in per-head rate charges the light eater exactly what the biggest appetite pays, whereas meals bought on the day are settled at whatever each person actually orders.
- What separately booked rooms cost last time: Rooms booked one at a time for the same nights differed by nearly 8,000 yen across the group last trip, while a building rented whole arrives as one bill that divides evenly.
- Time alone in the shared-house year: The year the group took a house together, whoever wanted an hour by themselves had nowhere to take it; a town with streets, shops and a public bath absorbs that easily.
- How last year's days ran: Last year the days ran separately and two of the group went from breakfast to dinner without meeting; a party that moves together shares the day whether it plans to or not.

## Plan
The discussion follows this plan.
- Round 1: The group discusses what information is needed to make a fair and comfortable choice. They focus on costs, travel logistics, and the balance between group time and privacy.
- Round 2: Participants share the findings from their research. They compare the financial implications, the time spent traveling, and the physical constraints of the accommodations.
- Round 3: The group weighs the trade-offs between cost certainty, travel time, and personal comfort. They evaluate which option best addresses the collective needs before voting.

Each participant's part:
- Victoria: Focuses on total cost predictability. She analyzes the financial data to avoid unexpected expenses.
- Toshio: Focuses on minimizing travel overhead. He evaluates the time spent in transit versus time at the destination.
- Daisuke: Focuses on the quality of the living environment. He examines the specifics of bathrooms and room layouts.
- Sakura: Focuses on the fairness of payment methods. She looks for arrangements where costs are divided equally.
- Midori: Focuses on the social dynamics of the group. She analyzes how the location affects their time together and alone.

Write the complete transcript of the discussion in the exact Markdown format specified. Output only the transcript.

## Output format
Markdown, exactly this structure; nothing before or after it:

# shared_living_0004
## Round 1
### Talk
#### Turn 1 of 4
- **<Name>**: <utterance, or exactly Skip, or exactly Over>
(one line per participant, in the fixed speaking order; repeat for Turn 2, 3 and 4; a participant who said Over has no line in the later turns of that round)
### Action
- investigate: <Name> -> <card title>; <card title>
(one line per participant; titles exactly as listed)
## Round 2
### Talk
(4 turns as above)
## Round 3
### Talk
(4 turns as above)
### Vote
- <voter name> -> <option label>
(one line per participant)
- adopted: <label of the option with the most votes>
## Result
- adopted: <label>
